plain_what: Like a starling that only watches its seven nearest neighbours, each step looks at a handful of earlier positions whose geometric 'frame' is closest to its own. It rotates their information into its own frame, takes their consensus and nudges its state toward it. No scores are normalised and no weights are multiplied.
how_it_works: Each 8-dimensional block keeps context in a ternary BinderPlan tree whose leaves are earlier positions; interior nodes hold the snapped sum of their three transported children. Every (block, tree level) has one Gate trit in {-1,0,+1}. Eligible nodes at a level end strictly before the query. They are ranked by (L1 distance between the node's frame root and the query's frame root, coordinate Hamming distance, recency, node id) and the best K (1 to 8) are kept. Each kept payload is carried into the query's frame by the BFS transport action between the two frame roots, the carried vectors are summed, and the sum is snapped to the nearest of 16 orbit roots: the level's consensus. Trit +1 adds the consensus root to the query payload, -1 subtracts it, 0 skips the level. The output is the query payload plus the added roots, snapped back to a root. This is the integer form of the Vicsek/Kuramoto rule Delta = K_h * (mean - v_t) with K_h in {-1,0,+1}: align with the local flock, with no weights, no normalisation and no division. Earlier float forms picked 7 neighbours among icosian vertices of the 600-cell (home vertex plus its 12 adjacent ones) with a learned rank table or content gate.
geometry: 16-root E8 orbit (frame roots and consensus snap); BFS transport actions between roots; SpiralCore ternary BinderPlan tree. Float-era forms: icosian vertices of the 600-cell with 12-vertex neighbourhoods, exact icosian quotient transport, Kuramoto/Vicsek alignment, Minkowski/Lorentz rank scores, Hamming rank on sign codes.

status_reason: The discrete Flock kernel passes 25 finite CUDA controls (docs/labs/discrete-driver-cost-2026-10-13/README.md) and runs inside every Relation and FrozenZero arm, since relation-off is bit-identical to Flock (docs/mechanisms/finite-relational-head.md section 3.3). No arm has isolated Flock's own value. The float starling and rank-table forms are inactive evidence (docs/mechanisms/README.md).
reopen_conditions: C1 (docs/harness/prep/m4-c1-flock-coupling-DRAFT-2026-10-18.md): a float-trained coupling magnitude K_h per (head, level) over the fixed integer Flock topology, exported to a Gate trit or small integer, with zero-coupling and random-coupling controls, 2 seeds or 200 fresh rows, and a reported export gap. Not yet registered.

C2: lawful soft-to-hard selection with a rank-consistent hinge and a linear or piecewise anneal (no temperature exponential) ending at the exact integer rank, scored by source-in-flock rate and rank-1-when-kept by distance bucket.
C3: FBS ternary-tree murmuration for O(log n) reads, only after C1 shows the coupling learns and gated on a long-context bar with tokens per second reported first.
Any retry of the float starling/rank-table forms needs a fresh FIT, an owner release, a separately scanned float module, a D11 integer export and no softmax surrogate or helper.

rule_compat.D11: Discrete kernel is gather/compare/add/subtract with snap built by repeated addition (discrete.cu); no float, no multiplier. The served integer flock selector exists for the old LUT stack (uor-r4-integer/src/stack/flock.rs); no D11 export of a trained discrete Flock artifact has been built or measured in the audited records.
rule_compat.D23: Discrete form compliant: hard rank by integer keys, no exponential. Rungs 1-3, the pivot and the surrogate used softmax helpers, surrogates, sigmoid/tanh gates or teachers and are inactive evidence; the M4 rank tables were trained with a flock-softmax straight-through gradient.
rule_compat.D30: Compliant in the discrete and rung-0b forms: no matmul. The float M4 stack that hosted rank-table runs is a dense transformer-style stack and is archived.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Discrete form is D32 integer, GPU-only and trained by counterfactual moves (held except owner-typed scoped releases). D37 permits a float-trained coupling (C1) only through a new FIT'd pre-registration with an integer export and reported export gap.

failed_only_on_configuration: Starling rungs 1-3, the pivot and the softmax surrogate: trained from scratch with a host-side selector, sigmoid/tanh gates, and softmax helpers or surrogates, on a synthetic 512-token recall task with a small model. They show that this recipe never learned the ranking; they cannot judge a hinge-credited integer flock.

M4 rank-table reads (+0.0185 to +0.2585 BPB): trained inside a softmax-tuned stack with a flock-softmax straight-through gradient, hyperparameters tuned for softmax, one W/K setting, host flock at 16-26k tok/s against 163k, short context. The 54% of the gap closed by the learned table was a stop recommendation that D22 reversed.
SoftSort S: closed by owner decision as not geometric enough and too costly, not by a measured negative.
Ring-store starling at 1,536: each cell kept only the last 4 keys, so the collapse is eviction, which the base-3 tree fixed.
Dose 1 and A8 Flock-equivalent controls: run on a 16-vector codebook or on cells that learning moved away from targets, so the read was never the thing being measured.
open_questions: Does a hard integer flock with only Gate-trit learning have enough capacity, or does it need a learned coupling magnitude (C1)?
How should a source outside the kept set receive credit without a softmax: exploration slots with a rank hinge (C2)?
Is one shared address per token (store and query) enough, and does cell occupancy collapse under it?
What is the right K, and does K matter once admission is fixed?
Can the tree (C3) keep recall flat to distance 1,000 in the integer form, as the float tree did?
related: route-read: Flock replaces Route's single leaf with a transported consensus of K neighbours
relation-read: Flock plus an exact-relation reranker; relation-off equals Flock
admission: every Flock-equivalent run so far was limited by admission before the read could be judged
rank-margin: the rank-consistent hinge that replaced the softmax surrogate in rung 0b
spiralcore-fbs: BFS transport and the ternary tree behind the O(log n) variant
hopf-observation: Hopf S3 to S2 observation considered for neighbour keys in the murmuration design
exact-memory: the persistent tree is an exact addressed store of the past
figure_ideas: A strip of token positions with the query at the right end. The K kept neighbours light up; for each, an arrow shows its 8-D payload being rotated into the query's frame; the arrows sum into one consensus point that snaps to the nearest of 16 orbit roots, and the query payload moves toward it.

Recall against distance (positions back) for three reads on one plot: ring-store flock (collapses past the last 4 keys per cell), tree flock (flat to distance 1,000), and softmax (flat at about 1.0), using the starling-context and starling-tree numbers.

The 600-cell drawn as 120 vertices; one token's home vertex and its 12 neighbours highlighted, with the 7 nearest earlier tokens inside that neighbourhood circled, shown beside the integer version that uses 16 frame roots instead.
